l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of First Instance set out the magistrate search-warrant threshold under Schedule 1 of the Implementation Rules.

l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of First Instance identified the core search-warrant challenge as whether specified evidence covers journalistic material.

l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of First Instance refused leave because the intended judicial review of the 2022 warrant was bound to fail.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal identified the central issue as whether specified evidence under the Implementation Rules covers journalistic material.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal recorded that the 2022 warrant specifically authorised search of digital contents including material claimed to be journalistic material.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that effective national-security investigation requires sufficient police powers and informs construction of specified evidence.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal treated Schedule 1 and local search laws as working in tandem as a coherent whole for NSL search powers.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that journalistic material is important but not immune from search and seizure in criminal investigations.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that specified evidence must include things, including journalistic material, likely to contain evidence of national-security offences.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / search warrants / seizure of digital or journalistic material
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that the judicial-review challenge to the 2022 warrant was doomed to fail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Affirms the CFI refusal of leave and directions giving effect to the 2022 warrant.
